items.item: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data.

at.step: Hook: the delete was correct, the name wasn't gone

items.item: Erasure must happen without undue delay once a listed ground applies.

at.step: Reveal: delete, expire, rewrite

items.item: Article 17(3)(e) carves out processing necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims.

at.step: Predict: which parts of the design were missing?

items.item: Cryptographic erase sanitizes the keys used to encrypt data, or the keys needed to access it, rather than the data itself.

at.step: Reveal: crypto shredding as the scalable alternative

items.item: A correct delete in one place isn't an erasure process; blind spots lineage can't see still need a named owner.

at.step: Reveal: the blind spots a register must name

items.item: Crypto shredding trades a per-subject key and a decryption lookup for every copy, including backups, going unreadable at once.

at.step: Reveal: crypto shredding as the scalable alternative

items.item: Proof of deletion is itself a deliverable this pipeline emits, not an auditor's job to dig up afterward.

at.step: Reveal: proof of deletion

items.item: The expiry schedule is itself the design decision, built to satisfy the legal deadline against the audit-retention window, not an afterthought to the delete operation.

at.step: Reveal: delete, expire, rewrite

items.item: A legal-claims carve-out is a lawyer's call the design makes visible and does not make itself.

at.step: Predict: which parts of the design were missing?

items.item: A replica placed in a region the erasure pipeline doesn't know about is exactly the kind of blind spot the register exists to catch.

at.step: Prove it: a replica in a second region

items.item: A subject index exists so a deletion can jump straight to the right files and partitions instead of scanning the whole lake.

at.step: Reveal: finding the data first

items.item: This topic leaves out the erasure mechanisms themselves, lineage collection and impact analysis, the legal analysis of what must be erased and when, and tenant-level erasure.
Composing table-format deletes, snapshot expiry, and crypto-shredding into one erasure process is each established practice, not an emerging technique.
This topic gives the shop a complete erasure process; the next design is the platform that watches the quality of the tags and lineage it depends on.
